post.caption: Bond's digital watch began as a prop. Stanley Kubrick wanted a futuristic watch for 2001, A Space Odyssey, and Hamilton Watch Company built one as a prop. Its research chief, John Bergey, helped turn the idea into the Pulsar. In 1970 he showed a prototype on The Tonight Show. The red display used so much power that the watch stayed dark until you pressed a button. The first Pulsar, in 1972, had an 18 carat gold case, and the first run of 400 sold out within days. In 1973 Roger Moore's Bond wore the steel Pulsar P2. Seiko bought the Pulsar brand in 1978.
